title: Computationally Efficient Tracking of Drifting Rare-Event Rates under Bounded Variation
banked_reason: D0.5 math and rubric PASS with all five cited leaves verified; cold general tier subfield below field floor, paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4, not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: Scope remains confined to deterministic Bernoulli paths within a public multiplicative rarity strip, a control arm with known unit second moment, and the fixed IPW estimator.

The reported enumerations check small component instances but provide no operational assessment of the active multi-epoch controller, usable risk constants, or finite-precision behavior, so the software application remains prospective.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved arbitrary-BV reflected-score stability, sharp unknown-variation tracking by a dyadic information-epoch likelihood master, lazy-affine resource bounds, and the original fixed-IPW causal transfer with matching statistical profiles. Both final substantive panels passed without findings and all five cited leaves were source verified; independent validity gates endorsed terminal downgrade because the subfield contribution scored 6.5 below the 7.4 field threshold. No F stage or Lean certification was performed; operational controller evaluation, usable constants, numerical stability, and broader models remain future work.
tldr: An explicit reflected-score tracker attains the sharp rare-Bernoulli bounded-variation risk budget \(F(n,\eta,w)\) simultaneously for every unknown variation budget, using \(O(n\log^2(2+n))\) exact-real scalar operations and \(O(n)\) words, uniformly as rarity vanishes. A Bernoulli likelihood master aggregates dyadic thresholds without an additional statistical logarithmic factor, and deterministic information epochs bound the combined tree storage. The established thinning and transfer results turn this tracker into a variation-blind original allocation controller attaining \(g(n,\rho,V)\); the fixed unbiased IPW estimator has excess MSE equal to precision regret divided by \(n^2\). The unrestricted statistical frontier and the efficient ALIGATOR reduction are supporting benchmarks.
gap: The precisely specified ALIGATOR reduction supplies a feasible rare-signal baseline with budget \(\mathcal A\), including \(\log^2(2+N)\) and \(\log^{4/3}(2+N)\) charges in its expected-risk partition derivation. That certificate does not settle exact rarity-uniform minimax attainment within a near-linear resource cap.
fill: The named minimax theorem and a positive or bounded negative resolution of the efficient-frontier question form the field-level deliverable. A positive result must derive every predictable update and resource charge at the exact budget \(F\), then meet the original controller contract at \(g\) through lawful thinning or direct likelihood. A bounded negative result must obstruct the quantified rate-and-resource contract on the relevant full class.
